word_studies.meaning: To afflict, humble, bow down low.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Daniel's fast was humbling himself before God. It's the same word as "afflict your souls" on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Fasting is humility, not a hunger strike to force God's hand.

word_studies.meaning: To hear with attention, to hear and respond.
word_studies.what_it_changes: God's hearing is never passive. He heard, and the answer was sent that same day.

word_studies.meaning: To stand, take a stand. Here with "before me": stood against me, face to face.
word_studies.what_it_changes: The prince stood in the way and blocked it. That's resistance, not refusal. The answer was already on its way.

word_studies.meaning: Prince, captain, chief, ruler.
word_studies.what_it_changes: The SAME word describes Michael in the same verse, "one of the chief princes." So the prince of Persia isn't the human king. He's a spiritual ruler on Michael's level, which is why the answer was held 21 days. See also Daniel 10:20 and Daniel 12:1.

word_studies.meaning: "Who is like God?"
word_studies.what_it_changes: His name is a question with one answer: nobody. The enemy said "I will be like the most High" (Isaiah 14:14). He's opposed by the angel whose very name says no one is.

word_studies.meaning: Desired, precious, treasured.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Before the explanation, before the battle report, God calls Daniel treasured. Said again in Daniel 10:19 and earlier in Daniel 9:23.

word_studies.meaning: To be strong, make firm, take hold.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Said twice, then Daniel says "I was strengthened," the same word. The command came with the power to obey it.

word_studies.meaning: Adversary, one who opposes. The verb means to resist, to accuse.
word_studies.what_it_changes: In Zechariah 3:1 he stands "to resist him," and that's the verb form of his own name. His name is his job description.

word_studies.meaning: Slanderer, false accuser. From a verb meaning to throw across.
word_studies.what_it_changes: He works by throwing accusations between you and God, and between you and other people.

word_studies.meaning: A prosecutor who brings charges in court.
word_studies.what_it_changes: It's a courtroom word, and yet we have a defense lawyer: "we have an advocate with the Father" (1 John 2:1), Greek parakletos G3875.

word_studies.meaning: Shining one, morning star. The root means to shine, and also to boast.
word_studies.what_it_changes: His name holds his glory and his fall at once: brightness that turned into boasting. Jesus is the real one: "the bright and morning star" (Revelation 22:16).

word_studies.meaning: A rock.
word_studies.what_it_changes: God is the Rock: "He is the Rock, his work is perfect" (Deuteronomy 32:4). Then: "their rock is not as our Rock" (Deuteronomy 32:31). Tyrus is the false rock set against the true one.

word_studies.meaning: To cover, screen, overshadow, protect.
word_studies.what_it_changes: It's the same word for the cherubim "covering the mercy seat with their wings" (Exodus 25:20). He was a guardian over God's presence, and he fell from there.

word_studies.meaning: Worthlessness, without profit.
word_studies.what_it_changes: His name means worthless. Everything he offers ends in nothing.

word_studies.meaning: Lord of the fly. The false god of Ekron.
word_studies.what_it_changes: King Ahaziah sent to Baalzebub instead of God, and Elijah asked, "Is it not because there is not a God in Israel?" (2 Kings 1:3).

word_studies.meaning: To cause to wander, to lead astray.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Our word "planet" (a wandering star) comes from the same root. Deception is a slow drift off course, not a sudden fall.

word_studies.meaning: To change the outward appearance, to disguise.
word_studies.what_it_changes: "Be ye transformed" in Romans 12:2 is a different word, metamorphoo G3339, a change from within. Satan changes his costume. God changes your nature.

word_studies.meaning: Destruction (Hebrew) and destroyer (Greek).
word_studies.what_it_changes: John gives the name in both languages so no one misses it: he destroys. Jesus came "that they might have life" (John 10:10).

word_studies.meaning: To fence in, to hedge about, as with thorns.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Satan admits the hedge is there. The enemy could see God's protection around Job before Job could.

word_studies.meaning: Literally "to bless."
word_studies.what_it_changes: In Job 1:11 and Job 2:9 the Hebrew literally says "bless God." It's a polite stand-in. The writer wouldn't put "curse God" on the page.

word_studies.meaning: To demand, to ask to have someone handed over.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Satan had to ask, just like with Job. And "you" is plural in Greek: he wanted all of them. "I have prayed for thee" is singular: Jesus prayed for Peter by name.

word_studies.meaning: To shake grain in a sieve.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Sifting separates. What's left after the shaking is what's real. Peter came out of it called to "strengthen thy brethren."

word_studies.meaning: Schemes, a planned method.
word_studies.what_it_changes: It's where our word "method" comes from. His attacks are strategic, not random. Look at Job: stacked and timed.

word_studies.meaning: Wrestling, hand-to-hand combat.
word_studies.what_it_changes: This is a close-range fight, not arrows from a distance. It's personal.

word_studies.meaning: First in rank, authorities, world-rulers.
word_studies.what_it_changes: These are ranks, a chain of command. That's exactly what Daniel 10 shows: a prince over Persia, another over Grecia.

word_studies.meaning: The heavenly realms.
word_studies.what_it_changes: It's the same word for where we're seated with Christ, "in heavenly places" (Ephesians 2:6). The battle is in that realm, and we're seated above it.

word_studies.meaning: To lose heart, give up, grow weary.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Jesus told the parable for one reason: so we don't quit while we wait.

word_studies.meaning: Literally to hit under the eye, give a black eye.
word_studies.what_it_changes: The judge was afraid she'd wear him out. If persistence gets through to an unjust judge, how much more to a loving Father.

word_studies.meaning: Shamelessness.
word_studies.what_it_changes: The friend got the bread because he wasn't embarrassed to keep knocking. Bold, shameless prayer.

word_studies.meaning: To wait, look for, hope. Also to bind together like a twisted cord.
word_studies.what_it_changes: The Hebrew doubles the verb: "waiting, I waited." It's the same word as "they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength" (Isaiah 40:31).

word_studies.meaning: Two different words. "Though it tarry" means to linger. "It will not tarry" means to be late.
word_studies.what_it_changes: It may linger from where you stand, and yet it will not be late on God's clock.

word_studies.meaning: Messenger. The same word translated "angel."
word_studies.what_it_changes: Paul's thorn was an angel of Satan sent to harass him, the same unseen conflict as Daniel 10.

word_studies.meaning: To strike with the fist.
word_studies.what_it_changes: It's the same word for what was done to Jesus: "and buffeted him" (Matthew 26:67). Paul suffered what his Lord suffered.

word_studies.meaning: To finish, complete, bring to its goal.
word_studies.what_it_changes: It's the word in "It is finished" (John 19:30). God's strength does its finished work in our weakness.

word_studies.meaning: To pitch a tent over, to dwell upon.
word_studies.what_it_changes: Christ's power doesn't just visit the weakness. It moves in and camps over it.

word_studies.meaning: To vindicate, to do justice for someone.
word_studies.what_it_changes: The martyrs aren't asking for revenge. They're asking God to prove them right. "Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord" (Romans 12:19).

word_studies.meaning: Incense, a burnt offering of sweet spices.
word_studies.what_it_changes: "Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense" (Psalm 141:2). Prayers are gathered and offered. None of them are lost.
